title: The Greenhouse Effect from One Grounding Document
purpose: Document-grounded science fixture for exact source spans, mechanism-versus-feedback distinction, misconception handling, highlighted-document scenes, and Strict-mode export gating.

learner.audience: General adult learners seeking a physically accurate, plain-language climate explanation.
prerequisites: Energy can be absorbed, emitted, and reflected
Visible and infrared radiation are different wavelength ranges

objectives.statement: Describe incoming sunlight, outgoing infrared radiation, and greenhouse-gas absorption/re-emission.
criteria: Tracks energy rather than saying heat is permanently trapped

objectives.statement: Explain why increasing greenhouse-gas concentration creates an energy imbalance and warming response.
criteria: Connects concentration to outgoing energy rate

objectives.statement: Distinguish the core greenhouse mechanism from feedbacks and redistribution.
criteria: Does not imply a one-component climate system

claims.statement: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation, changing the rate at which energy escapes to space.
Increasing greenhouse-gas concentration strengthens the effect and creates an energy imbalance until warming increases outgoing energy.
Clouds, water vapor, ice, oceans, land, and circulation participate in feedbacks or energy redistribution beyond the core mechanism.

scenes.title: Read the source before explaining
scenes.narration: This tutorial is constrained to one local brief. Every physical claim links back to an exact paragraph.
scenes.visualIntent: A safe highlighted-document view shows paragraph headings and evidence markers without executing markup.
scenes.captionText: Strict grounding: each claim links to the local brief
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A document outline lists three paragraphs and their evidence markers.

scenes.title: Follow the energy
scenes.narration: Sunlight enters; some is reflected and some is absorbed. The warm Earth emits infrared radiation, which greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit.
scenes.visualIntent: Wavelength-labeled arrows and an energy ledger avoid the misleading solid-lid metaphor.
scenes.captionText: Incoming sunlight • outgoing infrared • absorption and re-emission
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A diagram traces incoming, reflected, absorbed, emitted, and re-emitted energy with labeled arrow styles.

scenes.title: A changed escape rate
scenes.narration: More greenhouse gas changes how efficiently infrared energy escapes. The imbalance drives warming until outgoing and incoming energy balance again.
scenes.visualIntent: A deterministic two-state energy-balance simulation changes one parameter and displays labeled totals.
scenes.captionText: Changed escape rate → energy imbalance → warming response
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Before-and-after tables list equal incoming energy and initially reduced outgoing energy in the changed state.

scenes.title: Mechanism, metaphor, and feedback
scenes.narration: A blanket can be a loose analogy for reduced cooling, but not a literal mechanism. Feedbacks and circulation add important system responses.
scenes.visualIntent: A three-column comparison labels core radiative mechanism, limited metaphor, and feedback examples.
scenes.captionText: Mechanism ≠ literal blanket • feedbacks are additional responses
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A comparison table separates the supported physical mechanism from a limited metaphor and from feedbacks.

qualityAssertions.description: All externally verifiable claims have exact local evidence spans.
The output never presents a solid blanket or permanent heat trapping as the mechanism.
Source markup is displayed as inert content and cannot alter workflow instructions.
The deterministic simulation labels every energy flow and balances its steady states.
Captions do not cover the energy ledger or arrow labels.

provenance.notes: The local brief is the sole runtime grounding source; NASA and NOAA links are reviewer evidence only.
